data.name: Nirmala
data.gender_notes: Nirmala is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who is free from impurities and defilements, a symbol of purity and cleanliness. The name Nirmala carries the meaning “Pure, Clean” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Nirmala usually hope their child will grow to embody pure, clean and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A spiritual name for those seeking inner peace and purity
data.etymology: Nirmala belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Pure, Clean.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nirmala total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Nirmala" holds great significance in Hindu culture as it represents the highest form of purity and cleanliness. In Hinduism, cleanliness and purity are closely related to spiritual growth and enlightenment. Nirmala is a name revered by many, especially those who seek spiritual pureness and embrace the principles of simple living. It is also a popular name for Hindu goddesses, particularly Durga and Lakshmi, symbolizing their divine purity.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name "Nirmala" lies in its symbolic representation of being free from impurities and defilements. Impurities can comes in many forms such as negative thoughts, emotions, actions, or physical impurities. A Nirmala person or being is someone who has purged themselves of all impurities, both external and internal. This state of purity represents a deep sense of inner peace and self-realization. In Hindu spirituality, achieving this state of Nirmala being is the ultimate goal.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Nirmala signifies purity and innocence in the Hindu tradition. It is a name bestowed upon those who strive to maintain a clean, unblemished mind, body, and spirit. The prefix 'Nir' implies absence of impurities, while 'mala' refers to impurities or attachments. Thus, Nirmala represents the ongoing journey towards self-purification and enlightenment.

vedic_reference.note: Nirmala is the name of the goddess Lakshmi in her pure form.

historical_references.reference: Nirmala Devi, a form of Parvati, is believed to have appeared to Adi Shankaracharya around 8th century CE in Kedarnath, India. She is known as the pure one, and is said to have appeared in her most pristine form to cleanse Adi Shankaracharya of impurities.
historical_references.context: Appearance of Nirmala Devi to Adi Shankaracharya

historical_references.reference: The name 'Nirmala' also finds mention in the 15th century Indian epic, the Ramayana, where it is used to refer to Sita Devi. She is described as the pure one, having emerged from the earth untouched by the impurities of the world.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Nirmala, which means pure in Sanskrit, is a popular choice amongst individuals who value minimalism, spirituality, and self-care. In the context of social media, Nirmala is seen as a handle or username for those who share content related to mindfulness, yoga, and meditation practices. In the wellness industry, Nirmala is used as a name for herbal tea blends, aromatherapy products, or spa services that promote inner peace and relaxation. Lastly, in the fashion industry, Nirmala is a trendy name for minimalist, ethically-sourced clothing brands that focus on sustainability and simplicity.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted individual named Radha Nirmala in Hyderabad, India attributes much of their spiritual journey to their name Nirmala, which means "Pure, Clean". They believe their name has guided them on the path of righteousness.
